newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lazard bought 700 mln stg Eurotunnel debt.
newsitem.headline: Lazard bought 700 mln stg Eurotunnel debt.

text.p: Lazard Freres bought 700 million stg of the junior bank debt of Eurotunnel SA /Plc in the secondary debt market, Eurotunnel executive chairman Patrick Ponsolle told a news conference on Thursday.

Eurotunnel group treasurer Mike Grant said Lazard topped the list of its "main lenders" with a 8.71 percent holding, followed by the European Investment Bank with 4.28 percent, Bankers Trust with 4.27 percent and Merrill Lynch with 3.82 percent. The U.S. institutions bought the loans in the secondary market, he said.
The executives were giving details of its debt restructuring prospectus being sent to bank lenders and shareholders.

The next biggest debt holders are the four agent banks, National Westminster Bank Plc with 3.12 percent, Credit Lyonnais 2.95 percent, Banque National de Paris 2.95 percent, and Midland Bank 2.84 percent.
After those are the Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi with 2.49 percent and Bank of America, 2.37 percent.

The Japanese banks had been the biggest sellers of Eurotunnel's debt, and now numbered 10 instead of the initial 37 initial lenders. They now hold eight percent of the total stock of junior debt, compared to 19 percent, Ponsolle said.
The number of U.S. institutions has risen to 26 from 15 and hold 24 percent of the loans compared to four percent.
Eurotunnel's restructuring plan covers 69.4 billion francs of junior debt.

Grant said he did not know what price the banks had bought in the secondary market but the price had fallen as low as 25 percent of face value and were now apparently quoted at around 40-45 percent, he said.

Eurotunnel's British co-chairman Robert Malpas said the month-long window for official debt trading opened last month has made it easier to get bank approval for the restructuring: "Yes it has, absolutely, no question," he told Reuters after the news conference.
The number of French bank lenders has fallen to 35 from 39 and now hold 17 percent instead of 21 percent of the loans.
There are now 10 British banks in the syndicate, down from 15 and now hold 10 percent instead of 12 percent of debt.

A Eurotunnel executive thought it was likely the U.S. banks had bought a large part of the debt for their own account and some for investors, in order to receive the various financial instruments to be issued in the restructuring.
These banks have probably devised derivatives around these instruments which would give trading opportunities to funds without direct exposure to Eurotunnel itself, he said.

Eurotunnel plans to issue one billion pounds of equity notes, 1.2 billion stg of participating loan notes, and 1.5 billion stg of resettable bonds as part of the restructuring. It will leave in place four billion stg of junior debt, or 45.1 percent of the stock of loans.
"The purchase of debt by end-investors is reassuring," Christian Cambier, chairman of the Eurotunnel Shareholders Association, which group small investors, told Reuters after the news conference.

The restructuring prospectus lists 174 lenders of record compared to its original syndicate of 225 bank lenders. But some of those names included the same institution under the name of a related entity, said a Eurotunnel executive.
